questions.q: What did the people of Israel have to do in order to be blessed by Yahweh and to be set above all the other nations of the earth?
questions.a: The people of Israel needed to listen carefully to the voice of Yahweh and obey all his commandments.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do for the people of Israel if they will obey his commandments?
questions.a: Yahweh will enable them to defeat their enemies.

questions.q: What does Moses tell the people of Israel they will become if they obey Yahweh’s commandments?
questions.a: Yahweh will establish them as his own holy people.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do for the people of Israel if they will obey his commandments?
questions.a: Yahweh will send rain for their land at the right time and bless all their work.

questions.q: What will happen to the people of Israel if they will not listen to the voice of Yahweh and keep all his commandments?
questions.a: All the curses will come upon them.

questions.q: What will happen to the skies and the earth if the Israelites do not obey the commandments?
questions.a: The skies will not give rain and the earth will be as dry and hard as iron.

questions.q: What will happen to Israel when they fight their enemies if they do not obey the commandments?
questions.a: They will flee from their enemies and be defeated by them.

questions.q: What will Yahweh cause to happen to the people of Israel if they are disobedient?
questions.a: He will cause them to have boils, ulcers, rash, and itch, as well as madness, blindness, and mental confusion.

questions.q: What will happen if an Israelite is betrothed to a woman, builds a house, or plants a vineyard but disobeys Yahweh?
questions.a: Another man will rape his betrothed and he will not be able to live in the house or enjoy the fruit of the vineyard.

questions.q: What will happen to the sons and daughters of the Israelites if they disobey Yahweh?
questions.a: Their sons and daughters will be given to other peoples and they will not return to them.

questions.q: What will the people of Israel become among all the peoples?
questions.a: They will become a horror, a proverb, and a taunt among all the peoples.

questions.q: How will the disobedience of the people of Israel affect the crops which they plant?
questions.a: They will put seed in their fields and plant vineyards but they will not enjoy the harvest or fruit from them because the worms and the locusts will eat them.

questions.q: How will the foreigner become more important than the people of Israel?
questions.a: Foreigners will lend to them while the people of Israel will not be able to lend to the foreigners so will be considered inferior to them.

questions.q: What will happen because the people of Israel did not listen to the voice of Yahweh and keep his commandments?
questions.a: All the curses listed will happen to them until they are destroyed.

questions.q: Why will the people of Israel serve the enemies of Yahweh?
questions.a: They will serve their enemies because they did not serve Yahweh with joyfulness and gladness of heart when they had abundant blessings.

questions.q: What did Moses prophesy about the people of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh would bring a nation from far away to attack them with no respect for the aged or young, as well as taking their crops and animals, leaving them to starve.

questions.q: During the siege of the city what will the man who is described not share with even his own family?
questions.a: He will not give to any of them the flesh of his own children that he is going to eat.

questions.q: During the siege of the city what will a woman do with her own newborn and the children whom she will bear?
questions.a: During the siege of the city a woman will eat her own children whom she will bear.

questions.q: What will happen if the people of Israel do not honor the name of Yahweh by keeping the words in the book of the law?
questions.a: They will experience terrible plagues and enduring sicknesses.

questions.q: How many of the people of Israel will be left after Yahweh punishes them?
questions.a: Although they had been numerous, only a few of them will remain scattered among the other nations.

questions.q: Will the people of Israel find rest when they are scattered among the nations?
questions.a: They will find no peace or rest and they will be afraid, hopeless, and mournful.

commentary.text: Verses 1–14 This chapter is a very large exposition of two words, the blessing and the curse. They are real things and have real effects. The blessings are here put before the curses. God is slow to anger, but swift to show mercy. It is his delight to bless. It is better that we should be drawn to what is good by a child-like hope of God's favour, than that we be frightened to it by a slavish fear of his wrath. The blessing is promised, upon condition that they diligently hearken to the voice of God. Let them keep up religion, the form and power of it, in their families and nation, then the providence of God would prosper all their outward concerns.

If we do not keep God's commandments, we not only come short of the blessing promised, but we lay ourselves under the curse, which includes all misery, as the blessing all happiness. Observe the justice of this curse. It is not a curse causeless, or for some light cause. The extent and power of this curse. Wherever the sinner goes, the curse of God follows; wherever he is, it rests upon him. Whatever he has is under a curse. All his enjoyments are made bitter; he cannot take any true comfort in them, for the wrath of God mixes itself with them. Many judgments are here stated, which would be the fruits of the curse, and with which God would punish the people of the Jews, for their apostacy and disobedience. We may observe the fulfilling of these threatenings in their present state. To complete their misery, it is threatened that by these troubles they should be bereaved of all comfort and hope, and left to utter despair. Those who walk by sight, and not by faith, are in danger of losing reason itself, when every thing about them looks frightful.

If God inflicts vengeance, what miseries his curse can bring upon mankind, even in this present world! Yet these are but the beginning of sorrows to those under the curse of God. What then will be the misery of that world where their worm dieth not, and their fire is not quenched! Observe what is here said of the wrath of God, which should come and remain upon the Israelites for their sins. It is amazing to think that a people so long the favourites of Heaven, should be so cast off; and yet that a people so scattered in all nations should be kept distinct, and not mixed with others. If they would not serve God with cheerfulness, they should be compelled to serve their enemies. We may justly expect from God, that if we do not fear his fearful name, we shall feel his fearful plagues; for one way or other God will be feared. The destruction threatened is described. They have, indeed, been plucked from off the land, ver. #(63). Not only by the Babylonish captivity, and when Jerusalem was destroyed by the Romans; but afterwards, when they were forbidden to set foot in Jerusalem. They should have no rest; no rest of body, ver. 65, but be continually on the remove, either in hope of gain, or fear of persecution. No rest of the mind, which is much worse. They have been banished from city to city, from country to country; recalled, and banished again. These events, compared with the favour shown to Israel in ancient times, and with the prophecies about them, should not only excite astonishment, but turn unto us for a testimony, assuring us of the truth of Scripture. And when the other prophecies of their conversion to Christ shall come to pass, the whole will be a sign and a wonder to all the nations of the earth, and the forerunner of a general spread of true christianity. The fulfilling of these prophecies upon the Jewish nation, delivered more than three thousand years ago, shows that Moses spake by the Spirit of God; who not only foresees the ruin of sinners, but warns of it, that they may prevent it by a true and timely repentance, or else be left without excuse. And let us be thankful that Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, by being made a curse for us, and bearing in his own person all that punishment which our sins merit, and which we must otherwise have endured for ever. To this Refuge and salvation let sinners flee; therein let believers rejoice, and serve their reconciled God with gladness of heart, for the abundance of his spiritual blessings.
